subject: Learning Methods
title: Correcting Misconceptions Through Teaching
description: One-minute skill: Correcting Misconceptions Through Teaching.

hook.text: When a peer's question reveals a flaw in your explanation, the correction sticks in memory far longer than direct.

buildup.text: Self-discovered errors create surprise, and surprise strengthens encoding. Being told you're wrong is less memorable.

discovery.text: Teaching exposes misconceptions because a listener's confusion forces you to examine your own logic chain.

twist.text: Misconceptions are sticky. They resist direct correction. But the embarrassment of teaching them wrong is a powerful.

climax.text: Welcome the moment a student catches you in an error. That moment fixes the misconception more deeply than any textbook.

punchline.text: Teach wrongly, learn rightly. Errors caught while teaching stick.

quiz.question: Why do self-discovered errors during teaching stick in memory?
options: The social embarrassment triggers anxiety-based memory
Surprise at the error strengthens encoding more than being told
Errors during teaching are always conceptual, not factual
